children: With U.S. inflation moving sideways rather than downward, the debate about further tightening by the Fed is far from over, says Christian Scherrmann, DWS Chief U.S. Economist. Fed Chairman Warsh didn't comment on the outlook of monetary policy at a recent appearance, but other Fed officials have continued to send mixed signals. Their range of views suggests that the committee itself is divided on whether policy is already sufficiently restrictive, he says in a note. "Inflation remains uncomfortably high, but the combination of softer labor market dynamics and stable core PCE expectations argues for patience," he says. DWS therefore expects the Fed to leave interest rates unchanged in October while maintaining a hawkish bias. (monica.gupta@wsj.com)
